sections.title: Ultra Hard Concept
sections.content: Level 3 focuses on advanced Time & Work problems with multiple workers of varying efficiencies, fractional work, sequential & alternating tasks, pipes & cistern, and wages proportional to work done. Problems often require 3–5 step calculations and logical reasoning.

sections.title: Advanced Efficiency
sections.content: Efficiency = 1 / Time (days). For multiple workers, each may have a different efficiency. If worker A is d times faster than worker B, efficiency of A = d × efficiency of B. Multi-step problems may involve changing efficiencies over time or alternating work schedules.

sections.title: Combined & Sequential Work
sections.content:
• Combined Work: Sum all workers' rates, Time = total work ÷ combined rate.
• Sequential Work: Calculate work done in each segment: Time × Rate = Partial Work, then sum all partial works for total work.
• Alternate work: Workers alternate days; sum partial work per day until total = 1.

sections.title: Fractional Work
sections.content: If a fraction of work is already done, remaining work = 1 - completed fraction. Time for remaining work = remaining ÷ combined rate. Fractional work may involve complex multi-step calculations with multiple workers.

sections.title: Pipes & Cistern (Advanced)
sections.content:
• Filling rate = 1 / filling time, Emptying rate = 1 / emptying time (negative).
• Net rate = sum of filling rates - sum of emptying rates.
• Time = total work ÷ net rate.
• Fractional filling/emptying must be carefully considered for multi-step scenarios.

sections.title: Wages & Work Linkage (Advanced)
sections.content: Wages are proportional to work done. Individual share = individual work ÷ total work × total wages. For workers with different efficiencies, share = rate × time segment. Multi-step scenarios may involve alternating work, fractional completion, and variable efficiency.

sections.title: Important Formulas
sections.content:
1. Efficiency = 1 / Time
2. Combined rate = sum of all efficiencies
3. Fractional work: Remaining ÷ rate
4. Sequential/alternate work: sum of partial works
5. Pipes: net rate = fill rate - empty rate
6. Wages = proportional to work done
7. Time = total work ÷ net rate

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
• Forgetting to sum partial works in sequential or alternate tasks
• Ignoring ± in pipes problems
• Taking incorrect efficiency ratios
• Using wrong fraction for remaining work
• Wages miscalculated due to ignoring work done proportionally

sections.title: Summary
sections.content:
• Efficiency ∝ 1/Time
• Combined & sequential work: calculate segment-wise
• Fractional work: remaining ÷ rate
• Pipes: net rate = fill - empty
• Wages: proportional to work done
• Multi-step problems require careful stepwise solving

tricks.title: Multiple Worker Rate Shortcut
tricks.explanation: Add all workers' rates, then total work ÷ combined rate = total time

tricks.title: Sequential Work Shortcut
tricks.explanation: Compute partial work for each segment, sum them, total work =1
tricks.example: A 2 days, B 3 days, sum segment-wise = total work

tricks.title: Fractional Work Trick
tricks.explanation: Subtract completed fraction, then divide by rate to get remaining time

tricks.title: Pipes & Cistern Trick
tricks.explanation: Net rate = fill rate - empty rate, Time = total ÷ net
tricks.example: Fill 6 days, empty 12 days, Net rate=1/6-1/12=1/12, Time=12 days

tricks.title: Efficiency Ratio Shortcut
tricks.explanation: Faster worker rate = ratio × slower worker rate

tricks.title: Wages Quick Share
tricks.explanation: Individual share = individual work ÷ total work × total wages

tricks.title: Alternate Day Work Trick
tricks.explanation: Sum partial works for alternating workers until total work = 1
tricks.example: A,B alternate, Day1 A 1/4, Day2 B 1/5, sum until work=1

tricks.title: Multi-step Efficiency Tip
tricks.explanation: Solve each segment stepwise, then sum all partial works
tricks.example: Day1 A+B, Day2 B+C, total work = sum of partial works
